Description: An impact result whose test is unclear: the sheet names no test, or names both (a "Charpy" label beside an Izod standard, an "Izod" label beside ISO 179). Kept apart from Charpy and Izod and never compared; where the rest of the sheet points to one test, a reviewer's reading is written beside the value (impact_test_guesses.csv). A result whose own label or standard names the test is filed under that test.

Units: Shore A; Shore D; Rockwell M; Rockwell R; Shore (scale not specified by source)

Description: How much a moulded or printed part shrinks as it cools, to ISO 294-4 or ASTM D955. A sheet that prints it parallel and normal to the flow publishes two rows.
Resistance through the body of the material, to IEC 60093 or ASTM D257. It is what separates a conductive or ESD grade from an insulating one.
Resistance across the surface, to IEC 60093 or ASTM D257.
The field a material holds before it breaks down, to IEC 60243 or ASTM D149.
The dielectric constant, to IEC 60250 or ASTM D150. A sheet states the frequency it was measured at, which the row keeps as its test condition.
The voltage at which a wetted, contaminated surface begins to track, to IEC 60112. A sheet may print it as a stage rather than a voltage; only a voltage is a value here.
The least oxygen concentration that sustains burning, to ISO 4589 or ASTM D2863. A flammability class (UL 94 V-0, HB) is a certification claim, not this.

Not applicable reason: A tear test (ISO 34, ASTM D624) is run on elastomers and on tough, drawing plastics such as the polyolefins; a rigid filament is not tear-tested, and its sheet never prints one.
Description: The force per thickness that tears a specimen, to ISO 34 or ASTM D624. Published for elastomers and films.
The volume a standard abrasive removes, to ISO 4649 or DIN 53516. A smaller number wears less.

Not applicable reason: Compression set is how much of a squeeze a rubbery material keeps; a rigid plastic is not tested for it.
Description: How much of a compression an elastomer keeps after the load is taken off, to ISO 815 or ASTM D395. A sheet states the time and temperature, which the row keeps as its test conditions.
How much a specimen narrows as it is stretched.
Where the material begins to break down rather than melt, by thermogravimetry (ISO 11358). A sheet states the mass loss it is quoted at, commonly 5 %, which the row keeps as its test condition.
The stress a tensile bar carries at 5 % elongation, as a sheet prints it ("Tensile Strength @ 5% Strain"). Not a strength: no headline reads it, and it is never compared with one (D122).
The stress a tensile bar carries at 10 % elongation. Not a strength: no headline reads it (D122).

Not applicable reason: Only a material that stretches past 100 % has a stress at 100 % elongation: an elastomer, or a polyolefin that yields and draws; a rigid filament breaks long before.
Description: The stress a tensile bar carries at 100 % elongation: an elastomer's "100 % modulus" (ISO 37, ASTM D412, or ISO 527 on an elastomer). Not a strength: no headline reads it (D122).

Not applicable reason: Only an elastomer stretches to 200 % and is tested there; a rigid filament breaks long before.
Description: The stress a tensile bar carries at 200 % elongation. Not a strength: no headline reads it (D122).

Not applicable reason: Only an elastomer stretches to 300 % and is tested there; a rigid filament breaks long before.
Description: The stress a tensile bar carries at 300 % elongation. Not a strength: no headline reads it (D122).

Not applicable reason: Only an elastomer stretches to 400 % and is tested there; a rigid filament breaks long before.
Description: The stress a tensile bar carries at 400 % elongation. Not a strength: no headline reads it (D122).
A tensile-impact test (ASTM D1822, ISO 8256): a bar pulled to break by a pendulum. Neither a Charpy nor an Izod result, and compared with neither.

Applies to: Modifier / filler: Carbon fibre | Glass fibre | Aramid fibre | Natural fibre
Not applicable reason: Fibre content is the share of reinforcing fibre a maker adds to the plastic; a material sold without a fibre load has none to state.
Description: The fibre load the maker states, by weight unless the row says otherwise; a range is kept as printed.
